title: Practice Set STI3 — Exactly-Once Sinks
description: Mid streaming recognition track. Module 3 of 5 — exactly-once sinks.

datasets.description: Schema reference (sample rows). NordGrid Energy at mid scale; the CSV is a small sample for schema reference.

tasks.title: foreachBatch and the Idempotent Write Pattern

description.context: EXACTLY-ONCE semantics in Structured Streaming sinks works through TWO MECHANISMS together. The CHECKPOINT location records which Kafka offsets have been processed (or which input source positions have been consumed). The SINK's commit log records which batch IDs have been written successfully. On restart, Spark replays from the last checkpointed offset and skips batches whose ID is already in the sink's commit log. This works for built-in sinks (Delta, Kafka, file sinks) because they handle the commit log atomically with the write. For CUSTOM sinks via foreachBatch, the engineer must make the inner write IDEMPOTENT — typically by using the batchId argument as part of a deterministic key (so re-running batch 42 overwrites the same target rows, not append duplicates).
description.task: Why does this pattern achieve exactly-once at the JDBC sink, even though JDBC is not a Spark-managed sink?

evidence.title: Input sample
evidence.content:
Code: df.writeStream.foreachBatch(write_with_batch_id).start()

Sink: external JDBC table (Postgres) — not a Spark-managed sink

Checkpoint Location: s3://nordgrid/checkpoints/positions_aggregator

evidence.title: Dataset
evidence.content: NordGrid streaming pipeline using foreachBatch with batchId-based idempotency for an external JDBC sink

evidence.label: Plan output
evidence.content:
def write_with_batch_id(microbatch_df, batch_id: int):
    # Pattern: each row's primary key includes batch_id
    # so re-running batch 42 overwrites the same rows, not duplicates them
    (microbatch_df
        .withColumn('batch_id', lit(batch_id))
        .write
        .format('jdbc')
        .option('url', 'jdbc:postgresql://...')
        .option('dbtable', 'metrics')
        .mode('overwrite')
        .option('truncate', 'false')
        .option('createTableColumnTypes', 'batch_id INT, ...')
        .save())

q = (df.writeStream
        .option('checkpointLocation', 's3://nordgrid/checkpoints/positions_aggregator')
        .foreachBatch(write_with_batch_id)
        .start())

# What happens on restart after a crash mid-batch:
# 1. Spark reads checkpoint -> last successful batch_id was 41
# 2. Replays from Kafka offset stored at end of batch 41
# 3. Re-runs batch 42 (same input data, same batch_id=42)
# 4. JDBC overwrite with WHERE batch_id=42 replaces the partial write atomically
# 5. No duplicates emitted; exactly-once achieved at sink

fields.label: Why does this pattern achieve exactly-once at the JDBC sink, even though JDBC is not a Spark-managed sink?
options: Spark's checkpoint location stores all output rows alongside the offsets; on restart, Spark deduplicates rows already written. The JDBC sink itself plays no role; checkpoint deduplication handles everything.

The batch_id is deterministic — batch 42 reads same Kafka offsets. Combined with sink-side overwrite-by-batch_id semantics, re-running batch 42 replaces the partial write. Same batch_id, same output, sink overwrites instead of appending.
JDBC supports two-phase commit with Spark; the checkpointLocation triggers a 2PC handshake that prevents duplicate writes. Without checkpointLocation, the JDBC sink would write at-least-once.
outputMode determines exactly-once semantics; foreachBatch automatically uses append mode which deduplicates by row hash. Different output modes would produce duplicates; append is the safe default.
fields.correctAnswer: The batch_id is deterministic — batch 42 reads same Kafka offsets. Combined with sink-side overwrite-by-batch_id semantics, re-running batch 42 replaces the partial write. Same batch_id, same output, sink overwrites instead of appending.
fields.rationale: The exactly-once pattern in foreachBatch has two parts. (1) DETERMINISM: batch_id N processes the same input rows because checkpoint records Kafka offsets — re-running batch 42 reads same offsets, produces same rows. (2) IDEMPOTENT WRITE: the engineer's foreachBatch writes WITH batch_id as part of the target key, using overwrite-where-batch_id=N semantics. If batch 42 partially completed and crashed, restart re-runs and the sink overwrite REPLACES the partial write rather than appending. Spark provides exactly-once for INPUTS via checkpoint; the engineer's logic is responsible for OUTPUT.
fields.distractorRationale:
Option A: Treats checkpoint as output deduplication; checkpoint stores offsets/state, not output rows.

Option C: Invents 2PC integration; JDBC has no 2PC handshake with Spark.

Option D: Treats output mode as exactly-once mechanism; foreachBatch is mode-independent for exactly-once.

tasks.pssReference: PSI5 lesson 6 (foreachBatch and Custom Sink Idempotency), PSI4 lesson 5 (Exactly-Once Semantics via Checkpoint + Sink).

description.context: When a streaming pipeline restarts after a crash mid-batch, exactly-once depends on the sink's idempotency contract. If the engineer used foreachBatch with a NON-idempotent inner write (plain INSERT INTO without batch_id key, or HTTP POST without idempotency-key header, or Kafka producer without transactional config), partial writes from the crashed batch are NOT overwritten on replay — they are PRESENT. The replay then writes the same rows again. Result: duplicates in the sink. The checkpoint is doing its job (replaying from the right offset); the sink is the failure surface. This is one of the most-commonly-cited streaming production incidents: the engineer thinks 'I have a checkpoint, I am exactly-once' and discovers duplicates the first time the cluster crashes.
description.task: Why did duplicates appear, and what is the fix?

evidence.title: Input sample
evidence.content:
Code: df.writeStream.foreachBatch(append_to_jdbc).start()

Checkpoint Location: s3://nordgrid/checkpoints/positions

Incident: cluster crashed during batch 142 at 70% completion; restarted 30 seconds later

Observed Duplicates: ~700 duplicate rows in metrics table after restart

Expected: no duplicates if exactly-once was working

evidence.title: Dataset
evidence.content: NordGrid streaming pipeline that wrote duplicates after a 30-second crash mid-batch — sink is a non-idempotent JDBC append

evidence.label: Plan output
evidence.content:
def append_to_jdbc(microbatch_df, batch_id):
    (microbatch_df
        .write
        .format('jdbc')
        .option('url', 'jdbc:postgresql://...')
        .option('dbtable', 'metrics')
        .mode('append')                         # ← append, no batch_id key
        .save())

q = (df.writeStream
        .option('checkpointLocation', 's3://nordgrid/checkpoints/positions')
        .foreachBatch(append_to_jdbc)
        .start())

# Incident timeline
# 10:00:00  Batch 142 starts; ~1,000 rows expected
# 10:00:21  Batch 142 has written ~700 rows to JDBC
# 10:00:21  Cluster crashes (executor lost)
# 10:00:50  Cluster restarts; Spark reads checkpoint (last committed batch=141)
# 10:00:51  Spark replays from Kafka offsets at end of batch 141
# 10:00:52  Batch 142 re-executes; writes all ~1,000 rows again
# 10:00:55  metrics table now has 700 duplicates from the partial first write

fields.label: Why did duplicates appear, and what is the fix?
options: The checkpoint is corrupted — it should have recorded the partial 700 rows so Spark would skip them on replay. Fix: rebuild the checkpoint via .option('checkpointLocation.repair', 'true').
JDBC sink itself does not support exactly-once at all; only Delta and Kafka sinks do. Fix: switch the sink to Delta and use Delta's MERGE INTO for idempotent writes.

Append mode is non-idempotent. Spark replayed batch 142 correctly, but JDBC append simply added rows on top of the 700 partial rows. Fix: include batch_id in primary key with overwrite semantics for the inner write.
30 seconds is too short for a restart; Spark's recovery requires at least 60 seconds for the JDBC connection pool to clear stale connections. Fix: configure spark.sql.streaming.minRetryInterval=60s.
fields.correctAnswer: Append mode is non-idempotent. Spark replayed batch 142 correctly, but JDBC append simply added rows on top of the 700 partial rows. Fix: include batch_id in primary key with overwrite semantics for the inner write.
fields.rationale: Duplicates come from the sink's non-idempotent append. Replay timeline: Batch 142 first attempt wrote 700 rows then crashed. Restart replays from end of batch 141. Batch 142 re-executes producing the same 1,000 rows (deterministic from offset replay). JDBC append simply adds those rows on top of the 700 partial rows — net 1,700 rows, of which 700 are duplicates. Fix: include batch_id in the target's primary key, use overwrite-where-batch_id=142, so re-running batch 142 replaces its own partial write. Built-in Delta/Kafka sinks do this automatically; foreachBatch makes it the engineer's responsibility.
fields.distractorRationale:
Option A: Treats checkpoint as output-row tracker; checkpoint stores offsets/state, not output.

Option B: Treats JDBC as fundamentally not exactly-once; idempotent JDBC writes work fine.

Option D: Invents a connection-pool stale-time issue; not the cause.
